# duplicate-code

Fails a repo whose duplicated lines pass 1% of its scanned lines. A native Go clone-detection engine judges them: a generic lexer plus a rolling-hash detector in `go/internal/clonedetect`. Its thresholds are modeled on [jscpd](https://github.com/kucherenko/jscpd)'s, but no jscpd tool runs, and percentage parity with it is not the goal. It is on by default.

## Behavior

- Scans every tracked file with min-lines 5, min-tokens 50, tests, Markdown, and JSON included.
- Binary files are skipped, since they have no lines to compare.
- Files the repo's `.gitattributes` marks `linguist-generated` are left out.
- Lockfiles and build wrapper files are left out, as each [language module](../../internal/lang/langs/langs.go) or the [lockfiles](../../internal/lang/lockfiles) folder names them.
- Pass: duplicated lines stay at or under 1% of the scanned lines.
- Fail: over threshold — the check reports `ERROR: duplicate code is X% of scanned lines, over the Y% threshold`, then `path: N duplicated lines` for each file holding them.
- The engine is built into the check binary, so there is no external tool to install.

## Scope

The check compares files of one format, so a scoped run reads the changed files and tracked files sharing their endings. A file's ending is its extension, or its whole name when it has none.

An unscoped run reads every tracked file. The 1% threshold applies to the lines read, so a scoped verdict can be stricter than an unscoped one.

## Comments

Comments never count as duplication. The lexer drops each comment, from `//`, `#`, `/*` or `<!--` to its end, before it compares tokens. Two files sharing only identical comments pass, as a real run in requirement 0139 shows.

## Templates

A doc must repeat its template, so templates are left out. Any file [doc-template](../fitness-check-doc-template/README.md#what-is-a-template) treats as a template is skipped, in any folder. Docs built from one template are still compared with each other and with every other file.

## Escape hatch

For duplication that's a real, justified constraint, such as boilerplate a framework requires per type, wrap it in inline-comment markers. Don't force a refactor:

```
// duplicate-code:ignore-start
...
// duplicate-code:ignore-end
```

The older `jscpd:ignore-start` and `jscpd:ignore-end` markers still work as deprecated aliases, so repos that carry them keep passing.
